newsitem.title: INDIA: Israel threatens to uproot peace process - Arafat.
newsitem.headline: Israel threatens to uproot peace process - Arafat.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said on Monday that Israel had declared war against the Middle East peace process, and urged members of the Non-Aligned Movement to review their diplomatic ties with the Jewish state.
"The Israeli government is going through a war of aggression against our people," Arafat told a meeting of foreign ministers of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) in the Indian capital.

"It is regrettable that the Israeli government should take advantage of the United States veto twice in 10 days to continue on the path of aggression and challenge international legitimacy," Arafat said.
"It is a declaration of war against the peace process."
U.S. vetoes on March 7 and March 21 prevented action by the U.N. Security Council on Israel's plan to build 6,500 homes for Jews on land captured during the 1967 Middle East war.
Ties between the Palestinians and Israelis plunged into crisis after the Israeli government broke ground on the settlement.
Accusing Israel of seeking to convert Palestinian territories into "Israeli cantons", Arafat said: "This policy will uproot the peace process."

He appealed to the NAM delegates to help convene an early special meeting of the United Nations General Assembly to discuss the issue. He said recent meetings of the U.N. Security Council had failed to yield any result.

"Jerusalem is the core of the Palestinian cause, it is the key to peace and war in the region," Arafat said. "Peace will not be realised until Jerusalem returns to its legitimate owners as the capital of the independent Palestinian state."
Arafat urged NAM members to follow recent resolutions of the Arab League seeking to review diplomatic ties with Israel.

"These resolutions also have called upon the brethren and friendly countries which have initiated the process of establishing relations with Israel to link the progress in these relations with the degree of Israeli commitments to U.N. resolutions," he said.
Arafat's surprise appearance at the meeting in New Delhi was welcomed by the Iranian delegates, headed by Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati.
But an Israeli official, following the discussions, said Arafat's speech could harm the peace process.

"It was certainly not a very helpful speech," an Israeli diplomat told Reuters. "Instead of talking about negotiating with Israel, he is calling for severing ties with us. He is advocating terror tactics."
Indian Foreign Minister Inder Gujral welcomed Arafat's "thought-provoking account ot the developments in the Middle East".
"We assure President Arafat of our support for the realisation of the rights of the Palestinian people," he said to applause.

An Iranian delegate told Reuters: "We sympathise with the stand of the Palestinian leadership and the Arab stand against Israel. It is a belated acceptance of our view that Israel was never sincere about a just peace in the Middle East."
